body: This PR tracks ongoing fixes and issues discovered while testing. In addition, it adds a workflow with a build script to validate the generated artifacts.

comment_data.body:
## zizmor / 

credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts: does not set persist-credentials: false

[Show more details](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/security/code-scanning/92)

comment_data.body:
This might be a bit confusing if you wanted a normal mode ctrl-v, but I guess it is the only way to accept a paste in the standard browser security model..

Maybe a `ctrl+shift+v` or something can be passed through to nvim. alternatively, let nvim handle `ctrl+v` and use `ctrl+shift+v` to paste which seems to be allowed.

Also, is `metaKey`, how command gets represented on mac os?

> Also, is `metaKey`, how command gets represented on mac os?

Yes , metaKey maps to Cmd on macOS

comment_regular_data.body: Do you plan to add a CI job?

> Do you plan to add a CI job?

Yes, I plan to do that after fixing some issues in this PR.

For the official build artifacts, we should investigate adding a `wasm-opt` (from https://github.com/WebAssembly/binaryen) step to the pipeline. From tree-sitter experience, it then can be beneficial to skip optimization during the LLVM build step (`--no-wasm-opt`) and rely solely on a dedicated follow-up `wasm-opt` call (both for build time and final artifact).

I get the following message on startup, is this to be expected:

> log: "/home/user/nvim.log" not accessible, logging to: "/home/user/.local/state/nvim/logs/nvim.log"

Perhaps just removing the `$NVIM_LOG_FILE` setting is fine. Finding things in the expected XDG locations is not surprising.
it is common to get this error when opening files: as a simple workaround for now, the demo could add `"--cmd", "set noautoread"` startup parameters
nice! gonna merge this now so we can see nightly build triggers as expected..
